# AID IoT · DESIGN (DRAFT)

> **DRAFT. No visual decisions have been made.** The YAML block above is generated from `tokens/` by
> `npm run build` and holds placeholder values only. Prose below records what is confirmed and what is open.
> Format: Google Labs DESIGN.md (YAML tokens + prose, canonical section order, extra sections allowed).

## Overview
AID IoT designs and makes IoT products and solutions: hardware, software, or both. The brand is **a solver**:
it understands the problem statement before proposing anything; empathetic, clear, innovative and agile.
Admired for clarity: Apple (simplicity, sharp positioning); Siemens and Samsung (structure that non-technical
people follow). Audience detail: awaiting leadership.

## Colors
Placeholder only. `primary` maps to an orange sampled from the current logo, `accent` to its green; both are
labelled `placeholder-logo-*` in `tokens/palette.tokens.json`. A colour study will replace them.
- Use semantic roles (`color.action.primary.bg`, `color.text.primary`), never palette steps.
- Status colours are protected and identical across brands: never restyle `status.*`.
- Confirmed constraint: few colours. "Too many colours" is on the brand owner's dislike list.

## Typography
Two faces shared by every brand (decided 2026-10-30; details and loading in `core/fonts/README.md`):
- **Archivo** (text face): headlines, body, labels, captions, legal small print, and numbers inside sentences
  and headlines.
- **Atkinson Hyperlegible Next** (data face): anything a reader compares, checks or copies: table values,
  device IDs, registration numbers, coordinates, times, specifications, prices. Use `.aid-data` (or
  `.aid-data--strong` inside bold text); it matches height and weight to Archivo on the same line.
- Do: "Battery <span class=\"aid-data\">41%</span>" in a status line. Don't: set a whole sentence or a
  headline in the data face, or use the data face without `.aid-data` (it will sit too small and too heavy).
- Display may use an optional brand accent face (`brand.font.accent`) only if it earns its place.

## Layout
12-column grid, 4px spacing base, comfortable density by default. Placeholder values.

## Elevation & Depth
Open. No shadow tokens yet.

## Shapes
Shared core radii: `radius.control` (buttons, inputs), `radius.container` (cards, panels), `radius.pill`.

## Components
Core reference components (`core/components/components.css`) style themselves from semantic tokens. AID IoT
changes their look only through its tokens.

## Do's and Don'ts
- Do lead with the outcome in plain language; put engineering detail one level down.
- Do use semantic tokens; don't write hex values anywhere outside `tokens/`.
- Don't use category defaults: navy + orange glow, a device on a radial sweep, bento grids.
- Don't add noise, jargon, or anything that reads as AI slop.

## Imagery
AI imagery is the default (ChatGPT image generation, Figma); real customer sites cannot be shown. Save each
generated image with a sidecar `.md` holding the prompt. Imagery direction: open.

## Motion
Motion explains a mechanism; never decoration. Every animated component designs a reduced-motion state.
